ai-dataops-investigation-copilot.title: Investigating data pipeline incidents with an AI DataOps copilot
ai-dataops-investigation-copilot.summary: How InvestiNator links pipeline symptoms to inspectable evidence, human approval and recovery checks in a local demo.
ai-dataops-investigation-copilot.body:
What should a DataOps investigation copilot do?

An investigation copilot should connect pipeline symptoms to evidence, propose a bounded action and show whether recovery succeeded. A fresh dashboard can still show stale business data when an upstream consumer lags. Operators need evidence about affected datasets, owners and deadlines before deciding whether to replay, wait or escalate.

From a Kafka signal to an incident decision

  1. Collect telemetry and scope signals to the same time window and data flow.
  2. Correlate broker, consumer and freshness indicators. Keep evidence references with the incident.
  3. Use deterministic checks or optional AI assistance to propose a likely cause and next action.
  4. Have an operator approve the named action and confirm recovery against freshness and lag thresholds.

In InvestiNator, a local Kafka workload produces and consumes synthetic orders. ReplayLab supplies a disk-pressure scenario with correlated symptoms. The demo adapter emits recovery telemetry after the approved demo action. The project does not fill a real disk or restart a broker.

Trade-off and validation

A rule-only workflow is a useful control when symptoms and recovery are stable. AI assistance can summarize conflicting signals and retrieve a runbook when the pattern is unfamiliar. It introduces an extra failure mode, so the operator needs the original evidence and can decline the action.

Run the documented Compose demo and record the linked alerts, suspected cause, approval event and recovery check. The documented smoke script exercises the API workflow. Compare the time to first useful hypothesis with and without the assistant across the same replay fixtures. Report false approvals and unresolved incidents alongside speed. The local demo uses a fixed identity and simulated recovery. Production use would require real connectors, identity controls and operational validation.

What the business should measure

Start with median time to a supported diagnosis and the fraction of critical datasets that miss their freshness target during incidents. A proposed fix has value only when the people relying on that data can use it again.

cloudera-hdfs-object-storage-migration-r.title: Cloudera CDP migration readiness from HDFS to object storage
cloudera-hdfs-object-storage-migration-r.summary: A decision checklist for data inventory, Hive ACID, small files, cutover, and business acceptance.
cloudera-hdfs-object-storage-migration-r.body:
What should you verify before an HDFS migration?

Inventory the datasets and decide what equivalence means before estimating throughput. Record table owners, Hive table and transaction types, partition cadence, storage formats, file counts, protected data, downstream consumers and allowable interruption. Map Kafka, NiFi or Spark writers that may keep changing data during a copy.

Choose copy or rewrite by table class

  • For compatible external files, test a staged copy and register the new locations only after reconciliation.
  • For transactional tables, establish how to preserve the current logical data and update semantics. Validate source reads with the proper transaction-aware engine, then choose a supported target writer and table format.
  • For workloads with many tiny files, benchmark copy and compaction separately. Counts, list/request load and destination scan performance can move in different directions.

Measure whether the cutover is viable

Use a representative pilot with the same network path, engine versions and write patterns. Record bytes completed per hour, file and partition reconciliation, rejected data, runtime of representative queries, and impact on online workloads. Estimate catch-up using the measured net transfer rate after accounting for new writes. Keep a rollback window and make the original location available for reconciliation while cutover is evaluated.

Explain the decision in business terms

Compare the destination's storage, requests, compute, egress and operational support costs with the existing estate. Compare workload-level freshness and recovery objectives before approving the cutover. The checklist uses public patterns. Its throughput, compatibility and savings must be established for the intended environment.

Source: Cloudera Migration Assistant overview.

data-quality-foundation-for-ai.title: Data quality controls for reliable enterprise AI
data-quality-foundation-for-ai.summary: A practical release checklist for trustworthy retrieval, source freshness, permissions, and business impact in enterprise AI.
data-quality-foundation-for-ai.body:
Why does enterprise AI depend on data quality?

An enterprise assistant can sound certain while using a stale or incomplete record. On a policy query the result can be obsolete advice. On an operations query it can be a false escalation. Keep source ownership, freshness, permissions and traceability visible at answer time.

Put controls at ingestion and retrieval

  1. At ingestion, record source owner, last good update, coverage and sensitivity.
  2. At retrieval, apply document access rules and attach source version and timestamps.
  3. At answer time, require evidence for consequential claims. Abstain or route to an owner if sources conflict, are stale, or are unavailable.
  4. Log the decision and evidence identifiers so a reviewer can reproduce the outcome.

Validate a business failure case

Prepare a synthetic fixture with one delayed feed, a valid but superseded document, and a document restricted to a different role. Ask identical questions before and after applying retrieval controls. Compare supported-answer rate and escalation load. A correct answer in the restricted test should avoid revealing inaccessible data.

DataGuard AI is a related telecom data reliability MVP. It demonstrates missing and late feed detection, ETL health signals and estimated revenue at risk on seeded scenarios. Those examples illustrate why to surface upstream data failures. They do not demonstrate the performance of a retrieval assistant.

Decide what to release

Define minimum acceptable source coverage and freshness with the decision owner. Evaluate access violations and unsupported consequential answers before measuring adoption. Track review minutes per case and the cost of incorrect escalations to decide whether the control improves the business workflow.

from-ai-demo-to-production.title: A useful AI demo is not yet a production AI system
from-ai-demo-to-production.summary: A pragmatic checklist for moving an enterprise AI prototype toward reliable, governed and measurable production value.
from-ai-demo-to-production.body:
Define the business decision

Before choosing a model, define the user's workflow and current baseline. How long does the task take without AI? What error rate is acceptable? How will the solution reduce cost or risk? Without this baseline, a successful demo cannot establish return on investment.

Build a trustworthy data boundary

For retrieval systems, establish data ownership, document freshness, identity-based access control and source citations. For text-to-SQL, expose only permitted schemas, validate generated queries and use read-only credentials with strict execution limits. The model is only one part of the system.

Evaluate failures—not just successful examples

  • Correctness: test representative and adversarial questions against ground truth.
  • Security: check prompt-injection resistance, authorization, sensitive-data leakage and logging.
  • Operational resilience: handle timeouts, malformed outputs, rate limits and fallback paths.
  • Economics: measure cost per completed task, latency, escalation frequency and user adoption.
Architecture principle: Keep the model behind a controlled application boundary. High-risk actions require explicit policy checks and human approval.

Ship outcomes, not model screenshots

AI belongs in production only when the organization can demonstrate repeatable task success, bounded risk, observability, ownership and economic value. I would rather deploy a narrow assistant with measurable results than a broad assistant nobody can safely rely on.

gcp-data-quality-governance.title: Data quality and lineage on GCP with VerdaTrace
gcp-data-quality-governance.summary: A GCP reference platform that connects Pub/Sub, Python, BigQuery and Cloud Storage with source provenance and testable quality rules.
gcp-data-quality-governance.body:
What makes a dataset safe to use?

Before a dataset is used in a report or decision, the reader should be able to identify the source, time coverage, license, quality checks and processing steps. A dashboard should show whether a figure represents source observations or a deterministic fixture.

Architecture and decision

VerdaTrace documents a Pub/Sub ingestion path with a Python worker and BigQuery and Cloud Storage destinations. Versioned dataset definitions attach rules and source information. The executable flow reads the supported input, validates it, tracks lineage and produces a normalized result for analytics and the public portal.

A dataset registry adds work when onboarding a source. In return, it gives maintainers one place to decide what constitutes an acceptable row, where to quarantine invalid input and how to rerun the same logic. Let unknown license, sensitivity or coverage stay unknown until evidence resolves them.

Validation with actual and synthetic data

The public repository documents 72 attributed hourly Cairo weather observations from Open-Meteo, synthetic mobility data, and deliberately invalid fixtures. Run the repository's documented tests and demo build. Check that invalid input appears in quarantine, the report preserves the distinction between actual and synthetic sources, and the normalized output includes lineage and coverage.

Limitations and business use

The fixture and test evidence describe the reference implementation. They cannot establish a cloud SLA or cost at enterprise scale. On a real workload, measure onboarding time per source, invalid-row quarantine rate, and the share of reported metrics with traceable sources. Confirm warehouse and streaming costs with a representative workload before budgeting.

the-cost-of-untrusted-data.title: The most expensive data pipeline is one nobody trusts
the-cost-of-untrusted-data.summary: Why data reliability is a business risk, and how engineering teams can connect SLAs, ownership and incident costs to business outcomes.
the-cost-of-untrusted-data.body:
Start with the decision, not the dashboard

When a finance, marketing or operations team relies on data, the key question is not only whether the Spark job succeeded. It is whether the resulting data is fresh, complete, correct and ready before the decision deadline. A green scheduler does not prove any of those things.

Measure the cost of distrust

Trace every critical dataset to a decision owner. Capture when the decision must be made, how much delay is tolerable, and what happens when a metric is wrong. Revenue exposure, investigation effort, delayed campaigns and manual reconciliation are better measures of impact than raw task success counts.

Leadership question: What business decision breaks if this dataset is one day late, and who would notice first?

Design the operating model

  • Contracts: publish schema, freshness, completeness and acceptable-change expectations.
  • Observability: alert on data and business symptoms, not only CPU usage and failed tasks.
  • Ownership: connect each critical dataset to a human escalation path and a remediation playbook.
  • Recovery: make backfills safe, reproducible and verifiable against source totals.

Prove value through outcomes

Track mean time to detect, mean time to recover, percentage of critical datasets meeting SLAs, and the hours stakeholders spend reconciling numbers. A platform investment becomes defensible when it improves these measures at an acceptable total cost of ownership.

My rule of thumb is simple: reliability is not a technical luxury. It is what makes analytics usable—and AI trustworthy—when the organization needs to act.
